chapter: Booker Little and the Manassas circle
title: Booker's grief over Clifford Brown and joining Max Roach
summary: Booker returns to Memphis in tears after Brownie's death and later joins Max Roach; Charlie Haden calls him king of the eighth notes.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: ’56 I thought. Is that correct? I think ’56.

Anyways, when Brownie died, ’55 or ’56 he came back to Memphis. I was still ­ he came back in Christmas time and he said - he was crying. He said to me, man he said to me, “You know, Clifford’s gone.” He said, “Why couldn’t it have been me?” I don’t know young cats have that deep of a soul. He loved Brownie, you know, but he said, “Why couldn’t it have been me?”
So he was like prepared, you understand?
And he said he was a meteor, he went fast man. And so that was that. Then he would... Then Sonny knew of him, and Max had heard him through Brownie and all that.

And Max invited him to come and be in his band, and George, and stuff like that. George Coleman and he came out, and I was out in Cali now going to USC, and they would come out and we would go to jam sessions and turn the places out and stuff. I remember Charlie Haden made a little derogatory remark like, “That guy’s the king of the eighth notes.” You know, what he was doing with them eighth notes!
You know, not to get... Yeah. It falls as a complement. Charlie would call him “King of the eighth notes.” But what he was doing with those eighth notes is kind of like, you know.
